versions.short: The bill would revise a federal literacy grant program so that it prioritizes reading instruction based on the science of reading, which it defines as a body of evidence-based research identifying phonemic awareness, phonics, vocabulary, fluency, comprehension, and writing as essential to skilled reading. The bill would exclude from the program's comprehensive literacy instruction any approach that uses a three-cueing model, meaning teaching word recognition mainly through context, pictures, or sentence structure, or through visual memory. The bill would require the Department of Education and state educational agencies to give priority, when awarding these grants and subgrants to states and local school districts, to evidence-based activities aligned with the science of reading.
